items.title: Joseph Daley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 18, 2018
items.q: So if you came in to sub for Howard Johnson in the Gil Evans orchestra... Howard went in the Gil Evans orchestra. Gil would give him a fairly sophisticated part... So Howard would take that part and he would expand it. And then Gil heard it.

ctx.x: Well it’s quite a leap from that to the loft scene. And I wondered, as a tuba player, if you started listening to jazz, what did you think that your pathway into that music could be? Because you’re not hearing a lot of tubas unless you’re listening to New Orleans early, really early stuff, or I guess the opportunity presented by this new music.

Yeah most definitely. So again, like mentors and stuff, people that you run into that change your life and change your course in history. So in New York City like I said, I grew up on the Latin, you know, New York scene, on the lower east side, which was a big Latin mecca. So I was playing — I had a valve trombone that I was doing gigs on on the Latin scene, playing valve trombones. And during the weekend the Latin scene, you can do a gig, an early gig starting around maybe eight, then you move to another venue…

interesting things on the tuba. So he came in and he just like shattered my thoughts of what a tuba can do in a improvisational setting, or a setting where the music is not written down or structured and everything. Where I’m not playing a tuba part but I’m actually doing what the saxophones and everybody else is doing. I’m given the freedom to improvise and do all types of things. So Howard kind of reset my mind, and then I was also able to join his group at that time it was called Substructure. It was a group…
